questions.knowledge_point: Evaluating the Definite Integral of an Exponential Function
questions.worked_solution:
Taking the antiderivative and evaluating the difference at the bounds, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{3}{e}^{x}\,\text{d}x & ={e}^{x}\,{|}_{0}^{3} \\  & ={e}^{3}-{e}^{0} \\  & ={e}^{3}-1.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

questions.knowledge_point: Evaluating the Definite Integral of a Trigonometric Function
questions.worked_solution:
Taking the antiderivative and evaluating the difference at the bounds, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{\pi /6}^{\pi /3}(-{csc}^{2}⁡x)\,\text{d}x & =\operatorname{cot}⁡x\,{|}_{\pi /6}^{\pi /3} \\  & =cot\,(\frac{\pi }{3})-cot\,(\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}-\sqrt{3} \\  & =\frac{1-3}{\sqrt{3}} \\  & =-\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Evaluating the Definite Integral of a Trigonometric Function
questions.worked_solution:
Taking the antiderivative and evaluating the difference at the bounds, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡x{|}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-(-\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)) \\  & =0-(-1) \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Evaluating the Definite Integral of a Trigonometric Function
questions.worked_solution:
Taking the antiderivative and evaluating the difference at the bounds, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{\int }_{\pi /3}^{3\pi /4}(-{csc}^{2}⁡x)\,\text{d}x & =\operatorname{cot}⁡x\,{|}_{\pi /3}^{3\pi /4} \\  & =\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{4})-\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3}) \\  & =-1-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3} \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{3}+3}{3}.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Evaluating the Definite Integral of a Trigonometric Function
questions.worked_solution:
Taking the antiderivative and evaluating the difference at the bounds, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{\int }_{\pi /6}^{\pi /3}\operatorname{csc}⁡x\operatorname{cot}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =-\operatorname{csc}⁡x\,{|}_{\pi /6}^{\pi /3} \\  & =-\operatorname{csc}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})-(-\operatorname{csc}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})) \\  & =-\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}-(-2) \\  & =2-\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}} \\  & =\frac{2\sqrt{3}-2}{\sqrt{3}}.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
